System Map

The theme is not a list of separate trends. Four loops connect its parts: a data flywheel in which experiments produce data that improves the models that propose the next experiments; a verification brake in which more AI-made hypotheses add checking work and erode trust; a proof flywheel in which replicated results build the confidence that attracts more capacity; and an enclosure loop in which exclusive data deals give a model lead that wins the next deal.

LoopNameWhat it doesThis cycle
R1Data flywheel
Data and access		Experiments produce data, open and standard data improves models, better models propose better hypotheses, and better hypotheses get tested.Priming: open-data foundations funded
B1Verification brake
Proof and trust		More AI-generated hypotheses add verification work, unverified output erodes scientists’ trust, and lower trust slows the use of AI hypotheses.Turning: 89% spend time verifying
R2Proof flywheel
Lab capability		More lab capacity runs more experiments, replicated results build funder and regulator confidence, and confidence attracts more capacity.Priming: FDA accepts nonclinical data
R3Enclosure loop
Data and access		Exclusive data deals give a model lead, and a model lead attracts the next exclusive deal.Priming: one-year exclusive access

Hover over a status for its meaning: Priming means the parts are in place but the circle has not yet closed at scale; Turning means every step in the loop has current evidence, so it is running now.

The Scenario Matrix’s horizontal axis asks whether R3 Enclosure loop wins over R1 Data flywheel, that is whether lab capacity and data end up shared and open or private; its vertical axis asks whether R2 Proof flywheel overcomes B1 Verification brake, that is whether proof keeps pace with discovery.

What it means: the two loops a charity can push hardest are the proof flywheel and the data flywheel, and both turn on the same things: replication, open standards and verification. Speed is supplied by the outside switches, public money and cheaper AI, which the trust does not control. The levers it does control are what its grants pay for and what they require in return.
